decisive_items: Positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load (detected by real-time PCR)
Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test (from initial diagnosis)
response.rationale: The clinical presentation (bilateral keratitis, stromal immune ring, keratic precipitates, mild anterior chamber reaction) and systemic symptoms (fever, arthralgia) align with chikungunya virus infection. Definitive laboratory evidence includes positive aqueous PCR for chikungunya virus and positive IgM serology, while HSV, VZV, CMV, adenovirus, and rubella were all negative, ruling out herpes simplex keratitis and other viral etiologies.

rejected.why: Aqueous PCR was negative for HSV-1 and HSV-2, directly contradicting herpes simplex keratitis.
